recaps.title: Morning briefing
recaps.intro: The FAA ground stop fallout dragged into a second day with thousands of flights cancelled, while Microsoft said its outage was over. Elsewhere, the US lost its measles elimination status, Alaska elected a Democratic governor and Starship flew again.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: FAA ground stop disruption stretches into a second day with 3,000 flights cancelled
bullets.note: The Athletic reported the nationwide halt was lifted about four hours after it began Friday, but cancellations piled up.

bullets.text: Microsoft says access to its flagship software is fully restored after the global outage
bullets.note: The outage paralyzed systems around the world, Bloomberg reports.

bullets.text: The United States loses its measles elimination status
bullets.note: Measles cases nationwide have topped 5,400, according to CDC data cited by ABC News.

bullets.text: Trump tells advisers he may hold off on Iran attacks barring new provocations, sources say
bullets.note: Reuters cites sources on the president's thinking.

bullets.text: China and the US discuss tariffs and farm trade ahead of a Xi-Trump meeting
bullets.note: The talks were held at the first meeting of a new trade council, Reuters reports.

bullets.text: Canada and the US are making progress on a trade deal, Prime Minister Carney says
bullets.note: Carney gave the update on the trade talks.

bullets.text: Trump and other Quad leaders are set to meet in Manila on Tuesday, sources say
bullets.note: Reuters cites sources on the planned meeting.

bullets.text: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins the Alaska governor's race
bullets.note: NBC News projects the win flips the office from Republican control.

bullets.text: Alaska voters reject a measure to repeal open primaries and ranked choice voting
bullets.note: The state's unique election system stays in place.

bullets.text: SpaceX launches Starship on its 15th test flight, a planned 22-hour mission
bullets.note: SpaceX says the ship is healthy in orbit; the Super Heavy booster diverted to an offshore splashdown instead of a catch.

bullets.text: Supreme Court will consider Trump's order suspending asylum access at the southern border
bullets.note: The justices agreed to take up the executive order.

bullets.text: Police urge evacuation within a mile of a Peoria, Illinois, plant after a reported bomb threat
bullets.note: The threat was reported at BioUrja Renewables, formerly the ADM plant.

bullets.text: Hungary recovers 20 million dollars in cash in a probe of an Orban minister
bullets.note: The cash was recovered as part of the investigation, Reuters reports.

bullets.text: Kirkland Signature heavy whipped cream cans recalled over a possible cleaning chemical
bullets.note: Alamance Foods announced the voluntary recall.

recaps.title: AI & tech
recaps.intro: The Nvidia scandal kept widening, with new reporting on Jensen Huang, a CEO search and a sixth weekly stock drop. Anthropic heads into an IPO week as Google and Nvidia shipped new models.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang misled the company's top lawyer about an affair, sources tell Reuters
bullets.note: The Reuters exclusive adds to the scandal that ended his tenure.

bullets.text: Nvidia approaches Arm CEO Haas as employees seek Huang's return, media reports say
bullets.note: Reuters cites media reports on the CEO search.

bullets.text: Nvidia says it is still choosing a search firm to find Huang's successor
bullets.note: The company tamped down talk that it is already engaging candidates.

bullets.text: Nvidia shares fall 13 percent this week, a sixth straight weekly decline
bullets.note: Bloomberg says it is the stock's worst week in more than 18 months.

bullets.text: Key House Republicans request briefings from Huang, Nvidia's general counsel and a Commerce official
bullets.note: Congressional scrutiny of the scandal is widening.

bullets.text: Treasury Secretary Bessent blames Commerce for missing export controls on Nvidia partner Megaspeed
bullets.note: Megaspeed is the firm formerly led by the businesswoman at the center of the Nvidia scandal.

bullets.text: Anthropic will try next week to top SpaceX as the biggest public listing ever
bullets.note: CNBC says next week tests the AI trade, starting with Nvidia earnings and ending with the Anthropic IPO.

bullets.text: Dario Amodei says he hopes Anthropic will underpromise and overdeliver in its IPO
bullets.note: Amodei also named sourcing computing power as one of the company's biggest challenges, Bloomberg reports.

bullets.text: AI jumps to the top of worries about the financial system in the latest Fed survey
bullets.note: CNBC says the survey ranks AI risks as the biggest threat.

bullets.text: Nvidia releases GR00T 2, an open model for robotics research
bullets.note: Nvidia says it learns skills from human demonstrations that carry across different robot bodies.

bullets.text: Sundar Pichai lists a week of Google launches, including two new 8th-gen TPUs and Gemini 4 Carbon
bullets.note: The list also includes Gemini Robotics 2.5 and AlphaGenome 2 for disease research.

bullets.text: Google adds Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence in Gemini
bullets.note: It lets Gemini give more tailored responses using connected apps.

bullets.text: OpenAI says ChatGPT Wallet will not share actual credit card details with its AI agents
bullets.note: The Verge reports on how the payment feature protects card data.

bullets.text: Tesla invites select customers to buy the Cybercab for personal use
bullets.note: It opens the robotaxi to private owners, Reuters reports.

bullets.text: Epic Games adds to its legal lineup for a Supreme Court showdown with Apple
bullets.note: The app store fight is headed to the high court.

recaps.title: Sports
recaps.intro: The Spurs stretched their win streak to 11 and Dejounte Murray asked out of New Orleans. Svitolina stunned Sabalenka at the WTA Finals, and travel chaos pushed Oklahoma vs. Ole Miss to Sunday.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray wants a trade, and the sides are working on a resolution
bullets.note: His agent and team officials have started talks, ESPN reports.

bullets.text: Spurs win an 11th straight game behind a season-high 32 from Stephon Castle
bullets.note: San Antonio rises to No. 1 in the West and is 2-0 in NBA Cup group play.

bullets.text: Alperen Sengun scores a season-high 43 as the Rockets win
bullets.note: He joins Hakeem Olajuwon and Yao Ming in a rare Houston scoring feat.

bullets.text: Bam Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo each score 37 as the Heat win
bullets.note: Miami moves to 2-0 in NBA Cup group play.

bullets.text: Darius Garland's go-ahead and-one seals a one-point Clippers win
bullets.note: Garland finished with 24 points in the NBA Cup group game.

bullets.text: Deni Avdija scores 34 and Damian Lillard 29 as Portland wins a third straight
bullets.note: The Trail Blazers are 9-3.

bullets.text: 49ers WR Deebo Samuel will play Sunday, but Mike Evans is out with an Achilles injury
bullets.note: San Francisco faces the Cowboys.

bullets.text: Independent medical experts will review the care Eagles QB Jalen Hurts got for blood clots
bullets.note: The NFL and the players union will jointly pick the experts.

bullets.text: Kirk Cousins will start for the Vikings against the Packers on Sunday
bullets.note: Coach Kevin O'Connell made the announcement.

bullets.text: Predators win a seventh straight game
bullets.note: It was Nashville's seventh comeback win of the season; the Rangers also won in Vancouver.

bullets.text: Elina Svitolina beats Aryna Sabalenka 6-3, 3-6, 6-1 to reach the WTA Finals semifinals
bullets.note: Semifinals: Andreeva vs. Pegula and Noskova vs. Svitolina.

bullets.text: Oklahoma vs. Ole Miss moved to Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
bullets.note: Oklahoma's athletic director said the game was moved despite the school's strong objection.

bullets.text: NC State finalizes a five-year deal for Philip Rivers as head football coach
bullets.note: Rivers returns to his alma mater.

bullets.text: Arizona ends Auburn's 71-game non-conference win streak in men's basketball
bullets.note: It is Arizona's first SEC road win since 2016, ESPN says.

recaps.title: Vermont on X
recaps.intro: A showery, snowy weekend is starting, with mountain accumulations. Courts, a school-funding lawsuit and a Camel's Hump rescue led the rest of Vermont's news.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Scattered showers today, mostly snow but mixing with rain in the valleys
bullets.note: Modest accumulations are expected in the mountains.

bullets.text: Southern Green Mountains got 2 to 4 inches of snow while northern areas missed out
bullets.note: More rain and snow showers are expected through the weekend.

bullets.text: Vermont Supreme Court orders a new look at the dismissal of a murder case
bullets.note: The high court sent the dismissal back for another look.

bullets.text: A Vermont border crossing is closing for renovations
bullets.note: WCAX reports the crossing will close for renovation work.

bullets.text: Family sues Vermont in federal court over the 2025 education reform law
bullets.note: They argue it is unconstitutional to exclude religious schools from public tuition dollars.

bullets.text: Emergency GetWarmNowVT shelter program says it lacks enough indoor beds
bullets.note: “We just don’t have enough beds for folks to sleep in inside,” a program official said.

bullets.text: Sen. Bernie Sanders backs Chris Van Hollen for Senate majority leader
bullets.note: Sanders is among lawmakers supporting the challenge to Chuck Schumer.

bullets.text: Vermont officials and advocates explore second-look sentencing legislation
bullets.note: State officials and criminal justice reform advocates are discussing the idea.

bullets.text: Suspect in a Vermont elementary school threat is taken into custody
bullets.note: WCAX reports the suspect is now in custody.

bullets.text: Rescuers on snowshoes reach stranded hikers on Camel's Hump near midnight
bullets.note: Snowdrifts had buried the trail, Seven Days reports.
